description: Generator parameters for the synthetic benchmark (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2). Every parameter has a value, a source and a confidence level (§2.4). 'varied' parameters are swept in the sensitivity runs over 'range'; 'value' is the default run. Parameters without a source are marked confidence 'none' and are always varied.

people.source: Derived, not chosen (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.1): sample_size.minimum_people() with the generated world's REALISED minor share (44.4%) and family size (3.49 people, design effect 1.75) gives 31,104 (binding: minors' precision >= 0.999), rounded up. The 26 Oct assumptions (50% minors, 3 per family) gave 25,300 -> 26,000. The generator re-checks its own size on every run (summary.size_check). Gate G4 open: recalculated once the tolerances are agreed

origin_shares.source: BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.1: equal thirds so every origin reaches its slice minimum; results re-weighted to Dzaleka's mix afterwards

two_parent_share.source: none found; women and children are 93% of Dzaleka's population (situation research), so many households have one parent present

children_per_family.source: none found for Dzaleka; chosen so that families average about 3 people and about half of all people are under 18 (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.1). The realised shares are reported by the generator

mother_age_at_first_child.source: none found for the corridor; uniform range chosen for plausibility

birth_spacing_years.source: none found for the corridor; uniform range chosen for plausibility

parent_birth_years.source: Tuned 16 Nov 2026 with older_household_share so that minors are close to half (realised 44.5%) and people aged 50+ are a real slice (6.7%); BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.1. No corridor source

rw_father_element_q.source: Conflicting: HRW 1999 (most Rwandans do not share a family name) vs The New Times, 6 May 2026 (children traditionally take the father's surname); BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.2

bi_son_father_name_p.source: Disputed patronymic practice: Univ. of Burundi / Bigangara (1982) [B5]; BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.2

cd_parent_nom_t.source: DRC Family Code arts 56-62 allow passing a parent's nom with at least one different element; how often is unknown

rw_names_per_person.source: Profile rw-nec-2026.1, structure.names_per_person (NEC district council candidates)

cd_token_count.source: Profile cd-congonames-2026.1, structure.token_count_distribution (5+ tokens, 0.25%, folded into 4)

young_child_birth_year.source: Children born from this year draw their Kinyarwanda/Kirundi name from the newborn profiles (rw-nisr-2026.1; bi-derived-2026.1, low confidence), older people from the adult profiles

older_household_share.source: none found; added (16 Nov 2026) so that older adults, who have lower literacy and are more often written by ear (RESEARCH_LOG.md, 28 Oct), form a real slice

older_parent_birth_years.source: CENI 2025 profile birth decades start in the 1940s-1950s; range for older households

rec_records_per_person.source: BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.1: about 3 records per person, spread unevenly across sources

rec_source_shares.source: BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.3 lists the sources (MRZ rare); shares: none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_years.source: Record dates spread over the period of the current Dzaleka population's arrivals; none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_writer_language.source: Writer languages from CONCEPT-IDEA §5.4A (clerks, caseworkers, interpreters in Malawi: English, Chichewa; interpreters: Swahili, French, Kinyarwanda); shares: none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_writers_per_source.source: Number of distinct clerks per source and language, so shared-writer pairs occur (CONCEPT-IDEA §5.5A); none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_literacy.source: UNESCO UIS adult literacy 2022 by sex and youth 15-24 (RESEARCH_LOG.md, 28 Oct 2026). Rwanda from secondary sources only (to confirm). Conflicts kept in the log (DRC 68.5% in another series); no Dzaleka figure exists

rec_older_literacy_factor.source: Burundi adult literacy was 37% in 1990 (RESEARCH_LOG.md, 28 Oct), so people aged 50+ are far less literate than the 2022 average; factor chosen, varied

rec_by_ear_if_literate.source: Even literate people usually have their name typed by a clerk (RESEARCH_LOG.md, 28 Oct); share typed without seeing a written form: none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_convention_rate.source: Probability that a writer applies their own language's spelling for a sound (pack spelling_conventions); none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_confusion_rate.source: Base probability of a listener confusion per occurrence, weighted by the pack entry's confidence (high 1, medium 0.5, low/hypothesis 0.25); none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_foreign_name_rate.source: French-form names written by others: silent h, double letters, final vowel (pack rules); none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_christian_language_rate.source: Christian name written in the writer's language (crosspack attested forms, e.g. Jean -> John / Yohana); none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_free_variation_person.source: User's observation, 9 Nov 2026: families add, change or double letters because they like how it looks (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.3); no source on how often

rec_typo_rate.source: GeCo-style typing errors [B8]; none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_ocr_rate.source: OCR errors on printed or scanned lists [B8]; none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_postnom_dropped.source: DRC postnom often dropped outside civil records (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.3); CongoNames: 18% of exam records have 2 tokens; per-record rate: none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_nom_postnom_swapped.source: BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.3; none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_married_name_added.source: DRC Family Code art. 62: a married woman may add her husband's name; how often: none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_given_first.source: Local records write the surname first (Rwanda, Burundi, DRC exam lists; packs order_rules); English/French forms often put the given name first; shares: none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_missing_sex.source: none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_missing_age.source: none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_child_age_estimated.source: Children's ages are often estimated (GATE_EXAMPLES.md; 'about 10'); none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_age_heaping.source: Age heaping on multiples of 5 (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.3); 14% of dates of birth differ between linked records in South Africa [B14]

rec_missing_place.source: none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_place_other_period.source: Places renamed over time (Burundi 2025, Rwanda 2006, DRC 2015; places-2026.1): share of records giving the other period's name: none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_false_nationality.source: A false claimed nationality at a low rate (Duchaj & Ntihirageza 2009; NAME_CHANGE.md) [B18]; rate: none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_name_change_s1.source: NAME_CHANGE.md step 1 (given name replaced in exile; Duchaj & Ntihirageza 2009, Daley 2018); rate: none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_name_change_s2.source: NAME_CHANGE.md step 2 (surname also replaced), s2 < s1; rate: none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_adopted_name_used.source: Share of exile records (registration, distribution, school) that use the adopted name once it exists; none found; plausible value, always varied in the sensitivity runs

rec_error_scale.source: Calibrated 16 Nov 2026 on the full default world (31,200 people): one factor on all name error rates so that 22% of name values (surname, given names) differ between linked records of one person, the figure in South Africa [B14]; scale 0.15 gives 9.8% and 1.3 gives 35.3%, the sensitivity points of BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.4 test 4. Writers' spelling conventions are habits and are not scaled

invention.rule: A slot whose element is not drawn from a profile's listed (5+ times) elements is filled with an INVENTED element: a character-trigram chain trained on that slot's listed elements, rejected if it equals a listed element. The invention share per slot is the profile's uncovered share: 1 - (sum of listed counts / records). Christian given names are a closed set and are never invented: their uncovered share is drawn from the corridor-wide pool of listed Christian names of the same sex (all three profiles).
